records.title: Task dependency graph + Planner decomposition-independence prompt (ported from kandev/ccswarm research)
records.body:
## Summary

Port the task-dependency-graph pattern from kandev's `service_dependencies.go` into copilot-ui's task model, and tighten the Planner's decomposition prompt using ccswarm's independence-forcing pattern. Researched via cross-repo agent-orchestration analysis (kandev AGPL — reimplemented as a design reference, not copied; ccswarm MIT — ported closer to verbatim with attribution).

## Problem

The `pending → running → blocked | done` task lifecycle has a `blocked` state, but nothing in the spec currently defines *what* blocks a task beyond gate/loop failures. There's no way for the Planner (or a human) to declare "task B must not start until task A finishes," so PBI-derived tasks that have a real ordering dependency can only be sequenced implicitly (task order within a PBI), not enforced.

Separately, nothing in the Planner's prompt currently forces the tasks it emits to be safe to run independently — worth closing before the dependency graph exists, since without it the graph has nothing meaningful to encode.

## Proposed changes

**1. Task dependency graph (design reference: kandev `internal/task/service/service_dependencies.go`, AGPL — reimplement, don't copy)**

- Peer-to-peer `task_blockers` edges ("B depends on A"), distinct from PBI/task parent-child hierarchy — a dependency means "not until," not "part of."
- Blocked state **derived on every read, never cached/denormalized**. A stale `is_blocked` column is the exact failure mode this exists to prevent — the auto-start/gate-loop launch path must always compute it fresh.
- `AddDependency` is the single validator for all edges (self-edge rejection, cross-workspace rejection, cycle rejection) — every call site (task routes, any future API) goes through it so a second, weaker validator can't let a cycle in.
- Cycle detection via bounded BFS (`dependencyCycleWalkLimit`) — a walk that exceeds the cap rejects the edge rather than accepting an unverified one.
- Resolution requires the predecessor's terminal state to be **success** specifically — archived/pending/failed all count as unresolved. A chain must never advance on a failed step.
- Dependency gate fails **closed**: any read error on the blocker store returns blocked=true, not blocked=false.
- Deleting a predecessor unblocks dependents but does **not** auto-start them — deletion isn't success.

**2. Planner decomposition prompt (port near-verbatim: ccswarm `workflow/team_leader.rs::decomposition_prompt`, MIT)**

- Add an explicit instruction that generated tasks must be independently executable — modeled on ccswarm's phrasing: workers "do not see the other parts or this conversation," and the model should "use a single part if it is indivisible" rather than force a split.
- Apply ccswarm's defensive parsing pattern to the Planner's task-list output: tolerate markdown fences/prose around the JSON, drop empty-instruction tasks, de-duplicate IDs rather than fail the whole decomposition on a name collision.

## Out of scope

- kandev's webhook/PR-watch/CI-auto-fix-round-cap pattern — related but separate; will file as its own issue against the Committer/digest roles if this lands well.
- Any synchronous human-approval gating — contradicts the existing "human-out-of-the-loop by default" design principle (ORCH-REQ-012/013). Only the dependency-derivation and decomposition-prompt pieces are in scope here.
- Cross-agent file-level conflict prediction — none of the surveyed repos solve this; out of scope for this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AddDependency`/`RemoveDependency`-equivalent API with self-edge, cross-PBI/workspace, and cycle rejection, all validated through one code path
- [ ] Blocked-state read path has no caching layer; a test asserts a freshly-added edge is reflected on the very next read with no invalidation step
- [ ] Auto-start/gate-loop launch is gated by the dependency check and fails closed on a read error
- [ ] Planner prompt updated with the independence-forcing instruction; existing decomposition tests extended to cover malformed-JSON/prose-wrapped replies the way ccswarm's `parse_parts` tests do

## References

- kandev `internal/task/service/service_dependencies.go` (AGPL-3.0) — design reference only
- ccswarm `crates/ccswarm/src/workflow/team_leader.rs` (MIT) — `decomposition_prompt`, `parse_parts`

records.title: [PORTFOLIO] Tooling: Track release milestones and backlog execution order
records.body:
## User story

As the maintainer of ArchLinterNet, I want the public backlog to present release milestones as a clear product and architecture roadmap, so contributors and adopters can understand intended evolution without being overloaded by implementation tasks.

This issue tracks **releases and story-level initiatives only**. Detailed task graphs belong in owning stories/milestones.

**Portfolio milestone rule:** this long-lived roadmap issue is assigned to the furthest currently planned release milestone and moves forward when the roadmap is extended. Its own milestone is administrative and does not make the portfolio itself a v0.11 product feature.

## Release milestones

### v0.2.0 — Foundation before coverage

Stabilize validation, project discovery, adoption workflows, baselines and policy consistency before architecture coverage becomes a release gate.

### v0.3.0 — Coverage gate and Core stabilization

Deliver practical architecture coverage and restore a modular, testable Core execution architecture before broader rule-family growth.

### v0.4.0 — First-class boundary governance

Story-level scope:

- #104 — expand first-class architecture linting after coverage;
- #183 — stabilize extension hotspots and self-policy housekeeping;
- #247 — reduce accumulated SonarCloud technical debt.

Expected outcome: coherent assembly/project/package/public-API/placement/inheritance/metadata/composition governance with modular execution seams and trustworthy quality signals.

### v0.5.0 — Semantic policy foundation

Story-level scope:

- #106 — semantic architecture role discovery and contextual contracts;
- #279 — Makefile-style imports for the single root policy;
- #322 — reusable ArchLinterNet.CEL engine;
- #161 — CEL-compatible semantic policy expressions.

Expected outcome: deterministic **single-role** semantic classification, user-owned attribute/convention evidence, reusable role index, role/metadata selectors, modular policy composition and bounded CEL-backed predicates.

The single-role nature matters for later releases: a `ValueObject`, `Entity`, `Controller`, etc. does not become a second `ApiContract` role merely because it belongs to a reviewed compatibility surface.

### v0.6.0 — Adoption stabilization and deterministic analysis

Original v0.6.0 product increment was completed/published under #354.

Delivered foundations include deterministic build-state/preflight, immutable analysis sessions, normalized findings/identity, exact baselines, public API snapshots, policy imports, source sets, cache, profiling, cancellation, bounded parallel scanning and packaged schema/output consistency.

### v0.6.x maintenance and post-release engineering

Milestone 8 remains open for narrowly scoped 0.6-line maintenance and post-release engineering. Sharing the milestone does **not** mean every item blocks every patch release.

Current open story-level lanes:

- #527 — **v0.6.4 release authority:** connect already-delivered bounded type/architecture evidence to #94 public-API snapshot membership so adopters can replace whole-assembly API inventories with an intentional reviewed surface while preserving exact governance and existing semantic roles;
- #450 — post-release architecture cleanup/refactoring of v0.6 delivery hotspots and self-policy hardening.

Recently completed engineering lane:

- #474 — CI/dev-loop restructuring. Delivered context only; not part of open v0.6.4 dependencies.

#### v0.6.4 role-vs-membership boundary

#527/#525 intentionally distinguish:

- **semantic role:** one winning architecture classification from the v0.5 model;
- **reviewed public-API membership:** an orthogonal compatibility-surface decision selected from existing bounded evidence.

Primary orthogonal adoption path is a user-owned API marker consumed through already-delivered `has_attribute`-style matching, so a selected `ValueObject` can remain a `ValueObject`.

Release boundary:

- current published line is v0.6.3;
- next targeted patch is **v0.6.4 under #527**;
- #526 packed external-consumer gate is authoritative;
- #450/open refactoring does not block v0.6.4 unless a concrete dependency is explicitly added.

Expected v0.6.4 outcome: a modular consumer keeps CLR visibility and existing semantic classification unchanged, selects the real supported compatibility surface, deletes incidental implementation/domain/configuration signatures from the reviewed snapshot, and retains deterministic `api_comparison: exact` protection.

### v0.7.0 — Release Architecture Forensics and adjacent workflow/trust lanes

Primary product lane:

- #234 — deterministic Release Architecture Forensics from Git history: hotspots, co-change clusters, parallel-development bottlenecks, OCP pressure and evidence-backed refactoring candidates.

Complementary lanes:

- #116 — AI-first architecture drift workflow over complete authoritative results;
- #269 — verifiable NuGet provenance and artifact-integrity hardening.

Expected outcome:

- Git-range archi

records.title: Upstream proposal: Native parent-child relationships in beads
records.body:
# Upstream proposal: Native parent-child relationships in beads

**Parent**: #60 (RFC: Work Item Taxonomy)  
**Phase**: 3 (Long-term)

## Problem

Beads currently supports **dependencies** (`bd dep add`) but not native **parent-child relationships**. This means:

1. Epics and their tasks are linked via conventions, not schema
2. No built-in "get children of issue X" query
3. Progress aggregation requires external scripts
4. GitHub sub-issues can't be properly represented

## Current State: Dependencies vs Hierarchy

| Concept | Dependencies | Hierarchy |
|---------|--------------|-----------|
| Relationship | "A blocks B" | "A contains B" |
| Direction | Blocking direction | Parent → Children |
| Aggregation | No rollup | Progress/status rollup |
| Visualization | Dependency graph | Tree view |

## Proposed Enhancement to Beads

### 1. Schema Extension

Add `parent_id` and `children_ids` fields:

```json
{
  "id": "task-123",
  "title": "Implement feature",
  "parent_id": "epic-456",  // NEW
  "children_ids": []         // NEW (derived from parent_id lookups)
}
```

### 2. CLI Commands

```bash
# Set parent
bd parent set <child-id> <parent-id>

# Get parent
bd parent get <child-id>

# List children
bd children <parent-id>

# Create with parent
bd create "Child task" --parent <parent-id>
```

### 3. Query Support

```bash
# List all children of an epic (recursive)
bd list --parent <epic-id>

# List only direct children
bd list --parent <epic-id> --depth 1

# Show full hierarchy
bd tree <root-id>
```

### 4. Progress Aggregation

```bash
# Get rollup stats for parent
bd stats <parent-id>

# Output:
{
  "id": "epic-456",
  "children_count": 10,
  "children_closed": 7,
  "progress": 70,
  "status_rollup": "in_progress"
}
```

## API Design Considerations

### Option A: Explicit Parent Field

```go
type Issue struct {
    ID        string
    ParentID  *string  // nil for root issues
    // ...
}
```

Pros: Simple, clear semantics
Cons: Only single parent (no multi-parent)

### Option B: Typed Dependencies

```go
type Dependency struct {
    FromID   string
    ToID     string
    Type     string  // "blocks" | "parent-of" | "related-to"
}
```

Pros: Flexible, extensible
Cons: More complex queries

### Option C: Labels + Convention

```bash
# Current workaround
bd update child-123 --add-label "parent:epic-456"
```

Pros: No schema change
Cons: Fragile, no referential integrity

## Proposed Implementation Path

### Phase 1: Convention (Now)
- Document label convention: `parent:<id>`
- Add helper functions in Speckle scripts
- No beads changes required

### Phase 2: CLI Wrapper (Medium-term)
- Create `bd-hierarchy` wrapper script
- Implements `parent`, `children`, `tree` commands
- Uses label convention under the hood

### Phase 3: Native Support (Long-term)
- Submit RFC to beads repository
- Implement `parent_id` field in schema
- Add native CLI commands

## Draft RFC for Beads

```markdown
# RFC: Parent-Child Relationships

## Summary
Add native support for hierarchical issue relationships.

## Motivation
- Epic → Story → Task hierarchies common in agile
- GitHub/Jira/Linear all support sub-issues
- Progress aggregation needs structural support

## Proposed Changes

### Schema
Add optional `parent_id` field to issue schema.

### CLI
- `bd create --parent <id>` - Create with parent
- `bd parent set <child> <parent>` - Set parent
- `bd children <parent>` - List children
- `bd tree <root>` - Show hierarchy

### Behavior
- Circular references prevented
- Orphaned children allowed (parent deleted)
- Progress auto-calculated from children

## Alternatives Considered
1. Use dependencies with type (complex)
2. Use labels (fragile)
3. External mapping files (not portable)
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] RFC document drafted for beads upstream
- [ ] Label-based workaround documented
- [ ] Helper scripts created for Speckle
- [ ] Integration with GitHub sub-issues planned

## References

- [Beads repository](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads)
- [GitHub Sub-issues](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/adding-sub-issues)
- [Jira Issue Hierarchy](https://support.atlassian.com/jira-software-cloud/docs/what-is-an-issue/)

records.title: Adopt Symfony Finder for recursive MD5 file discovery
records.body:
## Summary

Add `symfony/finder` as an explicit production dependency and use it for the recursive file-discovery workflow in `cli/md5sum.php`.

Finder previously appeared in the vendored dependency tree only transitively. Production code did not use it and `composer.json` did not directly require it. Cacti now declares the component directly because it owns a production Finder call.

## Repository audit

A production PHP audit (excluding `include/vendor` and tests) found 21 traversal calls:

| Operation | Calls |
| --- | ---: |
| `glob()` | 5 |
| `opendir()` | 5 |
| `readdir()` | 5 |
| `scandir()` | 4 |
| `RecursiveDirectoryIterator` | 2 |

These calls implement roughly 12 distinct workflows. They should not all be converted.

## Implemented scope

Replace `cli/md5sum.php::dirToArray()` with a focused Finder-backed collector that:

- recursively returns files only;
- preserves hidden-file behavior;
- does not follow directory symlinks by default;
- applies Cacti's current ignore patterns to relative path names;
- preserves the historical manifest ordering: files at each level first, followed by child directories recursively;
- reports missing or unreadable roots;
- keeps stable relative path keys for MD5 generation and verification.

## Why Finder is used here

- Recursive traversal and filtering are the component's primary purpose.
- Relative path names come from the iterator instead of manual `substr()` calculations.
- Link-following policy is explicit.
- File-only selection avoids special-directory entries.
- The traversal policy is isolated and unit-tested independently from CLI/database bootstrap.
- The previous substring containment check could confuse a base path with a same-prefix sibling; Finder remains rooted at the configured input and does not follow the tested directory symlink.

## Why Finder is not used everywhere

- **Installer bootstrap:** recursive cleanup in `install/functions.php` must work when Composer dependencies are absent.
- **Hot poller loops:** Boost and poller cache scans are performance-sensitive and shallow; object-based traversal needs workflow-specific evidence before adoption.
- **Simple one-directory scans:** locale detection, package globbing, and log rotation have small native loops where Finder would add abstraction without improving correctness.
- **Existing SPL traversal:** `rrdcleaner.php` streams potentially very large RRA trees with SPL iterators; replacing it requires separate memory/performance evidence and explicit archive semantics.
- **Session directories:** session cleanup has permissions, races, and platform-specific behavior that require a separate security review.
- **Plugin discovery:** plugin ordering, integrated-plugin exclusions, and metadata/database side effects should be refactored separately before changing traversal.
- **Mutation:** Finder discovers files; deletion, copying, atomic writing, permissions, and moves remain Filesystem or native-I/O concerns.

## Dependency policy

- Declare `symfony/finder:^6.0`, compatible with Cacti's PHP 8.1 floor and existing Symfony 6 policy.
- Do not rely on a transitive installation as a production API guarantee.
- Do not commit generated lock-file or unrelated vendor updates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Declare `symfony/finder` directly in `composer.json`.
- [x] Add a focused, testable Cacti Finder collector for MD5 traversal.
- [x] Preserve current ignore, hidden-file, relative-name, manifest-order, and output behavior.
- [x] Add explicit symlink, sibling-prefix, unreadable-root, nested-directory, and ignored-file tests.
- [x] Demonstrate more than 80% coverage for new Cacti-owned Finder code (97.1%).
- [x] Run traversal performance checks on a representative large file tree (10,000 files: 0.174 seconds, 6 MiB peak after the compatibility-order comparator; the Finder object-sort prototype was rejected at 86 MiB).
- [x] Run PHP-CS-Fixer dry-run and PHPStan level 6 in Linux Docker.
- [x] Run the Unit and Integration suites in Linux Docker (1,614 passed, 4,034 assertions, 20 environment-dependent skips).
- [x] Verify the security sink inventory remains unchanged.
- [x] Document why the remaining 11 audited workflows stay native.

## Delivery

Implemented by draft PR linked below. The PR intentionally contains no generated Composer lock file or vendored dependency churn.

records.title: [GBB-FIX] REVIEWER-CANARY-F001 ancestry proof + ORCA gate
records.body:
# REVIEWER-CANARY-F001 — Fix Reviewer canary ancestry proof

Source fresh-context Reviewer decision: Issue #22 comment `5229307297` = `FIX_REQUIRED`.

## Finding to fix
F001 HIGH is valid against merged workflow commit `54af2033d23a044625b24ab46f4a308cd43219b2`:
- current code starts at `$PID` then searches `ParentProcessId -eq $parentId`, which walks children/descendants, not parents/ancestors;
- therefore `worker_service_count=0` does not prove the canary is not descended from a Worker service/process;
- forbidden regex omits `ORCA`.

## Exact base / branch
- exact base: `54af2033d23a044625b24ab46f4a308cd43219b2`
- implementation branch: `repair/reviewer-canary-ancestry-f001-r1`
- controller verified this clean branch starts exactly at the base above.
- Do NOT use abandoned branch `repair/reviewer-canary-ancestry-f001`.

## Executor
AI-B / ChatGPT Desktop LUNA as infrastructure implementation agent only. It is NOT the fresh-context Reviewer authority.

## Allowed paths — exactly two
1. `.github/workflows/reviewer-runner-canary.yml`
2. `tests/contracts.test.mjs`

No other tracked path may change.

## Required implementation
1. Preserve the existing identity/session gates and explicit `pwsh -NoProfile -File {0}`.
2. Replace/augment the current descendant-only logic with an explicit **ancestor traversal** starting from the current process and repeatedly following each process's `ParentProcessId` upward until PID 0 / missing parent / cycle guard.
3. Build a distinct ancestor process set that includes the current process plus actual ancestors.
4. Fail closed if any ancestor indicates Worker/Reviewer-boundary violation, including `GBBWorker` / worker-service ancestry.
5. Evaluate Windows services whose `ProcessId` matches the ancestor chain; fail closed if an ancestor service belongs to the Worker identity/path/service.
6. Add `ORCA` / `orca` to forbidden process/command-line detection.
7. Existing descendant check may remain as a separate defense, but it must not be mislabeled or used as proof of ancestry.
8. Emit deterministic evidence that distinguishes ancestry from descendants, e.g. `ancestor_count`, `worker_ancestor_service_count`, `forbidden_ancestor_count`; do not report a descendant count as ancestry proof.

## Required tests
Strengthen `tests/contracts.test.mjs` so it fails if:
- workflow has no explicit upward `ParentProcessId` traversal;
- ancestry is represented only by `Where-Object ParentProcessId -eq <current/parent>` child traversal;
- Worker-service check is not applied to the ancestor set;
- `ORCA` is absent from forbidden detection;
- `-NoProfile`, static `GBB-REVIEWER` routing, identity/session gates, no checkout, read-only permissions, and no model/browser invocation regress.

Tests must assert the contract semantics, not merely that the word `ParentProcessId` exists.

## Verification
Before READY_FOR_REVIEW:
- YAML parse: PASS
- `node --check tests/contracts.test.mjs`: PASS
- targeted Reviewer-canary contract test: PASS
- full `npm test`: PASS
- `git diff --check`: PASS
- base-to-head changed paths = exactly the two allowed paths
- no workflow dispatch / rerun / canary execution during implementation
- no Worker runner/service change
- no GBB/Chrome/ChatGPT/OpenCode/DeepSeek/ORCA execution

## Delivery
- one append-only implementation commit on the clean branch above;
- open a draft PR to `review-base/gbb-gh-01`;
- post strict READY_FOR_REVIEW bound to exact live PR head in this Issue;
- request a **new fresh-context ChatGPT 網頁版（GPT-5.6 Sol）Reviewer** to review the exact repair head.

## After code review PASS
Do not merge/dispatch automatically unless a later controller receipt explicitly authorizes activation. The old canary run `31288421120` / job `93181316507` remains historical evidence and MUST NOT be reinterpreted as proof for the repaired ancestry logic. A repaired workflow requires a new separately authorized canary execution/generation after merge.

## Blocked downstream
- Issue #24 OFFICIAL-REUSE-PROBE-00 remains HOLD.
- formal REVIEWER-00 remains blocked.
- Reviewer actuator remains blocked.
- ACT-02A remains blocked.

No Grok/Kimi review is required for this atomic implementation fix; independent fresh ChatGPT web review is the required authority gate.

records.title: Replace neo4j and the acts-as-dag closure table with Postgres recursive CTEs
records.body:
## Background

This project models its group/user/page structure as a time-dependent DAG. Because fast recursive queries were not available in Rails/Postgres at the time (see [graph-talk](https://github.com/fiedl/graph-talk)), the platform historically uses two graph backends side by side:

1. **acts-as-dag** (fiedl fork): the authoritative store. `dag_links` is a materialized closure table containing direct *and* transitive rows, with `count` path-bookkeeping and indirect membership validity ranges recomputed asynchronously by `RecalculateIndirectMembershipsJob`.
2. **neo4j 3.5 + neography**: an optional, callback-synced read replica (`your_platform/app/models/graph/*`), used by only three live queries (descendant memberships, officer page scoping, upcoming birthdays).

[graph_test_2026](https://github.com/fiedl/graph_test_2026) shows that at production scale (about 4k groups, 6k users, 36k edges), plain Postgres `WITH RECURSIVE` over direct edges outperforms the historic backends by orders of magnitude — node moves drop from days to about 2 ms. Since the migration to Postgres 17 (#124), everything needed is available: `WITH RECURSIVE`, the `CYCLE` clause, `range_agg`, `tstzrange`.

## Goal

Remove both graph backends and answer all transitive queries with recursive CTEs over direct edges only:

- neo4j, neography, the `Graph::*` sync classes, and the docker-compose neo4j service are removed entirely.
- `dag_links` keeps its shape (table name, `ancestor_*`/`descendant_*` columns, `valid_from`/`valid_to`), but stores only direct edges; the closure maintenance (`perpetuate`, `count`, indirect rows) goes away.
- Indirect membership validity switches from materialized min/max ranges to **episode semantics** (range intersection/union along paths), which also fixes the documented gap bug: a member who left in 2010 and rejoined in 2015 is currently shown as a member throughout 2010–2015.
- Obsolete machinery is deleted: `IndirectMembershipValidityRange`, `RecalculateIndirectMembershipsJob`, `DagLinkRepair`, and the closure-specific cache triggers.

## Staged plan

Each stage ships as its own CI-green PR:

1. Remove neo4j entirely (the three live queries get SQL replacements against the still-materialized closure).
2. Vendor the acts-as-dag fork into the engine so later stages can edit it with reviewable diffs.
3. Add the CTE query layer dark, with an A/B parity spec in CI and a `dag:verify_cte_parity` rake task for production-dump verification.
4. Cut non-membership traversal reads (ancestor/descendant accessors) over to CTE-backed relations; closure writes stay on.
5. Derive memberships: `group.memberships` becomes the direct memberships of the subtree; indirect memberships become read-only value objects with episode-based validity.
6. Stop writing indirect rows; delete the maintenance machinery; fix cache invalidation fan-out.
7. Delete indirect rows from production (with archive table) and drop the `count` column.
8. Optional cleanups: slim the vendored DSL, benchmark-gated cache teardown.

Expected net effect: about 2,000 lines of engine code and two dependencies (neography, acts-as-dag) removed, one docker service less, correct gap-aware membership history, and structural moves that no longer require closure rebuilds.

Co-authored by [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Claude Fable 5)

records.title: Performance improvements: more efficient dependency graph traversal
records.body:
**Background**
To determine the test files that need to be run, the plugin creates a dependency graph of all the files in the project (using `importlab`) with the test files as the origin nodes.

The directed graph representing the dependencies has edges `(u, v)` that is read as `u` depends on `v`. The origin nodes have no incoming edges (i.e. have no predecessors).

Currently the `pytest_git_selector.selector.select_test_files` function iterates through every node. The plugin checks whether that is one of the nodes representing a changed file. If that node represents a changed file, the plugin does a 'reverse' depth first search (i.e. it visits it's predecessor nodes rather than its descendant nodes). Nodes with no predecessors are the test files that need to be run.

**Potential enhancements**

1. It should be possible just to iterate only through the nodes that represent a changed file by looking up the nodes by name in the graph. `networkx` provides a dictionary interface into the nodes of a graph. See the [documentation](https://networkx.org/documentation/stable/reference/classes/generated/networkx.Graph.nodes.html).
2. We can keep track of visited nodes. This allows us to find the sources of the dependency graph more efficiently (in an amortized sense) by terminating a recursive call if that call starts at a visited node. Without this improvement, the cost of `m` calls to the recursive traversal function is `O(m * (|V| + |E|))`. With this improvement, we visit each edge and vertex at most once, reducing it to `O(|V| + |E|)`.

This is probably won't make much of a difference for small projects but may be noticeable for extremely large projects that have a dense dependency graph.

records.title: Feature: replace the heuristic `Sort-DependsOn` with a real topological sort
records.body:
## Summary

`Sort-DependsOn` in the `Parse` pipeline rule phase attempts to order DSC resource blocks by their `DependsOn` references using repeated array manipulation rather than a proper graph algorithm. It does not detect cycles, does not handle transitive dependencies correctly, and silently produces wrong orderings for non-trivial dependency graphs. A configuration with a cycle will loop indefinitely (or until a hard iteration limit is hit), and a configuration with a diamond dependency will apply resources in an arbitrary order.

---

## Current implementation (simplified)

```powershell
# Repeatedly move items with unresolved DependsOn to the end
do {
    $changed = $false
    foreach ($item in $sorted) {
        if ($item.DependsOn -and ($item.DependsOn | Where-Object { $resolved -notcontains $_ })) {
            # move $item to end of $sorted
            $changed = $true
        }
    }
} while ($changed)
```

This is O(n³) in the worst case and does not terminate on cycles.

---

## Problems

| Problem | Effect |
|---|---|
| No cycle detection | Infinite loop (or hard cap hit) on circular `DependsOn` |
| Transitive deps not resolved | Diamond graph produces wrong order |
| O(n³) complexity | Slow on large configurations |
| No error on unresolvable graph | Silently applies in wrong order |

---

## Proposed implementation

Replace `Sort-DependsOn` with Kahn's algorithm:

1. Build an adjacency list and in-degree map from the `DependsOn` keys.
2. Seed a queue with all nodes whose in-degree is 0.
3. Dequeue, emit, and decrement the in-degree of dependents; enqueue any that reach 0.
4. If the output list is shorter than the input, a cycle exists — throw a terminating error naming the cycle members.

This is O(V + E), detects cycles, and produces a correct topological order.

---

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Sort-DependsOn` (or its replacement) produces a correct topological order for a linear chain, a diamond, and a wide fan-in graph.
- [ ] A cycle in `DependsOn` throws a terminating error that names the resources involved in the cycle.
- [ ] An unresolvable reference (a `DependsOn` pointing to a resource not in the configuration) throws a terminating error.
- [ ] Pester tests cover: linear chain, diamond, fan-in, cycle, and missing-reference cases.
- [ ] Performance: a configuration with 500 resource blocks with random dependencies completes sorting in under 1 second.

records.title: Silent content corruption: reference resolution keys resolved content by name only, so same-named references to different artifact versions overwrite each other
records.body:
## Description

**Registry Version**: snapshot (main branch, 3.3.2-SNAPSHOT)
**Persistence type**: sql (also affects kafkasql, which delegates to the same SQL content repository)

Artifact reference resolution in `SqlContentRepository.resolveReferencesRecursive()` builds the map of resolved reference content keyed **only by the reference's `name` field**, instead of by the full artifact coordinate (groupId, artifactId, version).

Cycle/dedup detection separately tracks a `visited` set keyed by the full coordinate (`buildReferenceKey()` = `groupId:artifactId:version`), but that coordinate-based key is never used for the actual output map. As a result, if two references anywhere in the same reference tree share the same `name` but point at **different** artifact/version targets, one silently overwrites the other in the resolved-content map - with no warning, error, or log emitted.

Root cause, `app/src/main/java/io/apicurio/registry/storage/impl/sql/repositories/SqlContentRepository.java`:

```java
// ~line 339: dedup check uses reference NAME, not the GAV-based referenceKey
if (!resolvedReferences.containsKey(reference.getName())) {
    unresolvedReferences.add(reference);
    visited.add(referenceKey);
}
...
// ~line 391: final map is written keyed by NAME only - a second reference
// with the same name silently clobbers the first reference's content
TypedContent typedContent = TypedContent.create(content.getContent(), content.getContentType());
resolvedReferences.put(reference.getName(), typedContent);
```

A sibling implementation, `RegistryContentUtils.recursivelyResolveReferences()` (lines ~109-115), has an explicit, still-unresolved TODO acknowledging this exact hazard:

```java
* TODO: Currently, we stop tree traversal only based on the reference name.
* But what happens if the same reference name is used to refer to two different artifacts in different branches of the tree?
* We should use the target GAV to stop the traversal.
```

This confirms the bug class was known, but the batched SQL implementation (added later in the reference-resolution performance refactor, PR #7310) reproduces the same flaw without even a TODO.

This resolved-reference map is consumed by content dereferencing, compatibility rule evaluation, content validation, and canonical-hash-based dedup (`ConfiguredContentDereferencer`, `ConfiguredCompatibilityChecker`, `ConfiguredContentValidator`, `RulesServiceImpl`), and is reachable from REST v2/v3 (`GroupsResourceImpl`, `AbstractResourceImpl`, `IdsResourceImpl`) as well as the Confluent-compat API layer.

### Environment

- Plain Apicurio Registry instance (SQL storage), no Kubernetes/special deployment needed to reproduce.
- Reproducible via the REST API directly (no serdes client required).

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create artifact `Common` with version `1` and version `2` (different content).
2. Create artifact `A` that references `Common@1` with reference name `common.avsc`.
3. Create artifact `B` that references `Common@2` with reference name `common.avsc` (same name, different version).
4. Create a top-level artifact `Main` with two direct references: to `A` and to `B`.
5. Fetch/dereference `Main` (e.g. via the REST API dereference endpoint), or trigger canonical hash computation (`SqlVersionRepository.getContentHashRaw(canonical=true)`) - both call `resolveReferencesRaw` internally.
6. Inspect the resolved-reference content used: only one of `Common@1` / `Common@2` is present under the key `common.avsc` - the other is silently missing, even though `A` and `B` each declared a distinct, correct reference.

### Expected vs Actual Behaviour

**Expected**: Each reference's resolved content is tracked independently by its full artifact coordinates, so two distinct targets are never conflated just because they share a `name`. At minimum, a name collision between different GAVs should be detected and rejected or logged.

**Actual**: The reference resolved second for a given name silently overwrites the one resolved first, with no error, warning, or log line. Downstream consumers (dereferencing, compatibility checks, canonical hashing) then silently operate on the wrong referenced schema content for one branch of the reference tree.

### Logs

No error or warning is logged when this occurs - that is itself part of the bug. The nearest related log lines are debug-level cycle-detection messages (`log.debug("Skipping already-visited reference to prevent cycles: {}", referenceKey)`), which are not emitted in this scenario since the colliding references have different GAVs and are not caught by cycle detection.

records.title: EPIC: Quality-review tracking — July 2026 comprehensive review (53 issues, dependency graph, waves)
records.body:
**The dashboard issue.** Indexes all 53 review issues (conveniently, issue number = the review's P-number), carries the dependency graph, and tracks completion via the checklists below.

**Status — 2026-08-20: 49 of 53 closed** (all closed as completed; none abandoned). Remaining: **#50, #51, #52, #53** — the wave-5 documentation sweep, and the last four issues in the epic. All four human-decision gates have been answered. The IPC epic (#60) is sequenced after this one finishes.

Defects found *by* this work and filed outside the original 53. **Closed: #147** (the renderer pinned its vertex-attribute table one slot at a time, so `pos`/`uv` could swap silently) and **#148** (a documented test command that could not work — and `cargo check --benches` in CLAUDE.md §7, which compiles zero benches because the root package owns no bench target).

Still open: **#144** (animated `CustomMutation`s start on the browser and never tick), **#146** (`CachedConnection::translate`'s cap translation is covered by no test), **#153** (`DragState::Panning` carries no origin), **#155** (five `_ =>` subverb dispatch arms alias a newly declared subverb onto an existing behavior), **#156** (`help` is the only verb that never calls `kvs::read_strict`), **#157** (the overlay shape cache's single reuse key means a position-only change re-shapes instead of patching), **#158** (visual and on-device smoke — **explicitly not agent-closable**), **#160** (a touch-only user has no route to `FastResizeStart` since `TwoFingerDrag` was retired) and **#163** (doc comments can name a deleted non-test identifier and no gate notices).

## Background

A full-depth review of baumhard, mandala, maptool, and mandala_derive was performed in July 2026 against the project's own conventions: ten parallel area reviews plus a cross-cutting SSOT sweep, with all high-severity findings independently re-verified (several empirically). Baseline: 2669 tests green at commit `59cd115`. Synthesis, per-area evidence reports, verification log, and machine-readable manifest: [`reviews/2026-07-comprehensive-quality-review/`](https://github.com/Svendsys/mandala/blob/claude/repo-quality-review-qm6p15/reviews/2026-07-comprehensive-quality-review/README.md) (branch `claude/repo-quality-review-qm6p15` until merged; consider merging that branch so the evidence links go stable).

Sizing: **task** = small sharp fix · **feature** = one coherent PR · **[EPIC]** = staged multi-PR checklist.

## Model routing

- **Opus** — judgment-dominant work: subtle correctness semantics, API/framework design on load-bearing seams, or staged architectural surgery with real regression risk.
- **Sonnet** — well-specified single-PR execution: the fix plan already pins the design.
- **Haiku** — mechanical sweeps and post-decision policy toggles only.

All decision-gate issues (#15, #43 part C, #45, #47 part C) have been answered and closed; no gate blocks any remaining item.
